lockup.summary: Directors, executive officers and holders of almost all shares cannot sell for 180 days after the prospectus date unless J.P. Morgan and Evercore agree in writing.

what: A clinical-stage drug company developing medicines for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases using immune cells called Tregs found in tissue.
proceeds: It will use the money, plus its existing cash, to fund Phase 2 trials of TRB-061 (about $90.0 million) and Phase 1 testing of TRB-071 (about $10.0 million). The rest is for general business needs.
risks: It is an early-stage company with a short history and no approved products, and it has lost money in every year except one.
Raising more money may reduce existing owners' stakes, limit how the company operates, or force it to give up rights to its drug candidates.
It depends heavily on the success of its two main drug candidates, TRB-061 and TRB-071, and their trials may fail.
Delays or trouble signing up and dosing patients in trials could hold up or block regulatory approval.
Serious side effects from its drug candidates could delay or block approval, or hurt acceptance and cause problems after approval.
